The proposed solution claims that the minimum strictly positive fractional revival time \(t^{*}\) is always \(\pi\), independent of the prime \(p\). However, the spectral structure of the unitary Cayley graph \(\text{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{2p},\mathbb{Z}_{2p}^{\times})\) depends on \(p\); its eigenvalues are sums of roots of unity over the set of units, which vary with \(p\). Consequently the revival periods (which are determined by the common rational multiples of the eigenvalue differences) also depend on \(p\). The claim that a universal value \(\pi\) works for all odd primes contradicts this dependence and does not match known results for small cases (e.g., \(p=3\) where the graph is the 6‑cycle and the fractional‑revival time is \(\pi/2\), not \(\pi\)). Therefore the final answer is incorrect.  

**VERDICT: REJECT**
